reading.body:
Meta does not publish the power capacity of its Prineville campus. The campus sits in Crook County, Oregon, where it has been under development since 2010 with over $2 billion in total investment. Meta reports that the campus will employ 350 or more in operational roles and has committed its electricity use to 100 percent clean and renewable energy as part of its net-zero operations globally, with a separate Meta-supported project adding 977 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity to Oregon.

Because the campus power figure is not published, its rank among Oregon facilities cannot be derived from its own specification. Oregon has eight facilities with published power capacity totaling 156.6 megawatts, and 133 mapped facilities overall, most of which do not disclose their power draw. The state context ranks this campus ninth by published megawatts, which appears to reflect an earlier or interim figure not currently visible on Meta's official data center fact sheet.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on its actual power capacity, which Meta has not disclosed publicly. The presence of sustained multi-billion-dollar investment, peak construction of 1,000 skilled workers, and explicit renewable energy procurement suggests material scale, but the binding constraint on AI is compute and power, and without a published figure, this campus cannot be evaluated against other sites in the state or the grid.
